assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new classification of band matter based on invariants rather than broken symmetry. The Kane-Mele quantum spin Hall proposal, the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe prediction and the Molenkamp-group transport observation form a clear theory-to-experiment chain. The concept has spread through condensed matter, photonics and cold atoms, and it is original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall in graphene). Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental confirmation in HgTe. This supports a fair three-person configuration, but the supplied credit omits other theorists (for example Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and the 3D topological insulator discoverers, which is a real allocation problem I cannot resolve from the list.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed for over a decade in several materials and by many techniques (transport, ARPES). The interpretation is stable and the field is mature, so recognition is timely or overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or also cover 3D topological insulators, which would broaden the credit beyond the supplied names.
The size of the topological-insulator literature makes the boundary of the discovery uncertain; I have not independently checked the priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Active-matter hydrodynamics showed that collections of self-propelled units can show true long-range order in two dimensions, giant number fluctuations and new universality classes. Vicsek's minimal flocking model and the Toner-Tu theory give a compact nonequilibrium analogue of the Mermin-Wagner circumvention. The idea is simple, original and general, and it reaches from bird flocks to bacterial suspensions to engineered colloids.
assessment.attribution: The Vicsek model (numerical, 1995), the Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory (1995, 1998) and the Ramaswamy-type hydrodynamics of active suspensions are distinct, complementary contributions. The three credited names cover these strands reasonably, though Marchetti, Lauga and others also shaped the field, so I see the allocation as defensible but not airtight.
assessment.maturity: Theory is well developed and quantitative experiments (colloidal rollers, vibrated granular matter, bacteria) confirm key predictions such as giant number fluctuations. Some predicted scaling exponents remain debated in experiment. The field is established and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Experimental confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents is partial and system dependent.
Credit is spread over many contributors beyond the three names; the committee would have to decide which strand is decisive.
My own research is adjacent (active matter, stochastic dynamics), which could bias my familiarity upward; I treat the facts here as uncertain where I have not checked them.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters. The Jaksch-Zoller proposal and the Mott-insulator observation of Greiner and Bloch turned atomic physics into a controllable quantum many-body simulator, and later quantum-gas microscopes gave single-site resolution. This links atomic physics to strongly correlated condensed matter and has produced concrete insight into many-body dynamics.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac provided decisive theory, Greiner and Bloch the decisive experiments (superfluid-Mott transition, microscopy). Four names are credited, so a prize needs at most three: I pick Bloch, Greiner and Zoller as an experiment-plus-theory trio, but dropping Cirac is a judgement call, and Cirac is also credited under another ballot entry.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and used across many laboratories for over twenty years. The concept is mature. The open question is whether the simulations have yet solved problems beyond classical computation, which affects how much weight to give the applications.
uncertainties: Which of Cirac and Zoller, and which experimentalists, are decisive is uncertain.
Overlap with the trapped-ion and Rydberg-array candidates, and with the 2001 BEC and 2012 Wineland-Haroche prizes, could complicate how the committee frames the citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases (Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry phase) are a unifying concept across quantum mechanics, molecular physics, optics and condensed matter, and they underlie Berry curvature, the quantum Hall effect and topological band theory. The ideas are original and conceptually deep, and their impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Berry's 1984 adiabatic phase and Aharonov-Bohm's 1959 effect are the two decisive contributions, and the two credited names fit a two-person prize. Other precursors (Pancharatnam, Mead, Simon, Wilczek-Zee) complicate the history, and the prize might be seen as covering two distinct discoveries.
assessment.maturity: Both effects have been verified experimentally many times, and the interpretation is stable. The delay is very long, so the question is more whether it is overdue than premature.
uncertainties: The case combines two discoveries decades apart, so a single citation may be awkward.
Precursor priority claims (Pancharatnam, Mead and Truhlar) are not resolved by the supplied credit.
One credited person may no longer be able to receive the prize; I cannot verify the current status of either name.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform for flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity, and it started the moire materials field. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave a quantitative prediction that experiments then confirmed, a strong combination of theory and experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction of the magic angle (2011). Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experimental observation of correlated states and superconductivity. These three names fit a fair theory-plus-experiment configuration, though Cao and Fatemi (first authors) and Dean's and Kim's groups also contributed and are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups, but the origin of the superconductivity and the correlated phases are still under debate. The field is young, about eight years, so recognition would be somewhat early, yet the impact is large.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in the magic-angle system is not settled.
Credit for the experiment may reasonably include junior co-workers not named in the supplied list.
Possible prematurity compared with older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski equality extend the second law to small, driven, far-from-equilibrium systems by giving exact relations between work fluctuations and free-energy differences. They are exact, general and conceptually simple, and they give foundations for stochastic thermodynamics. This is statistical physics I know well, and I regard it as important.
assessment.attribution: Evans-Cohen-Morriss, Gallavotti-Cohen, Jarzynski and Crooks all made contributions, and the supplied credit names three of these. Crooks, Cohen, Morriss, Kurchan, Lebowitz-Spohn and Seifert are not credited, so the priority picture is crowded and the allocation is difficult to settle fairly.
assessment.maturity: Verified in single-molecule pulling experiments and in small colloidal and electronic systems, and widely used. The theory is stable, but the applications are in the realm of small systems and less visible than other candidates, which makes it somewhat slow to enter the prize canon.
uncertainties: Crowded priority picture; the three-person limit may leave out essential contributors.
Whether the committee views the result as a discovery of physical principle or as a useful mathematical identity.
I may be biased towards statistical-physics topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, and they are used for tests of relativity, geodesy and searches for varying constants. The magic-wavelength lattice idea of Katori is original, and Ye's group demonstrated record accuracy with strontium. This is high-precision measurement of lasting value.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and Ye's group did the decisive high-accuracy realisation. The two credited names form a clean pair. Hall and Hänsch were already honoured in 2005 for the frequency comb, which was an enabling step, and Ludlow, Zelevinsky and others contributed to the strontium work.
assessment.maturity: Many independent clocks confirm the performance, and redefinition of the SI second is being considered. Maturity is high, but the field is still developing and the redefinition may be a natural moment to recognise it.
uncertainties: Overlap in subject with earlier prizes (frequency combs 2005, ion clocks 2012) may reduce novelty in the committee's view.
Ion-clock groups (for example Wineland's) and other lattice-clock groups are not in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller 1995 proposal showed how to do quantum logic with trapped ions, and Blatt's group and others implemented gates, entanglement and small algorithms. Trapped ions remain a leading platform for quantum computing. The work is original and has had large impact on quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the key theoretical proposal. Blatt is one of several experimentalists (others include Wineland, Monroe, Wineland group's NIST work, Innsbruck and Oxford groups) who realised it, so the experimental credit is spread out. A fair three-person configuration is possible but the experimental names are contestable. Wineland's 2012 prize overlaps the experimental side.
assessment.maturity: The platform is well confirmed by many groups, but the quantum computing application is still unfinished. Recognition might be somewhat early for the computing claim, while the control of ions is established.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for measurement and manipulation of single quantum systems.
Attribution of the experimental implementation is contested between several groups.
Quantum computing's long-term importance is not yet settled.
